title: Axon Stretch Growth: The Mechanotransduction of Neuronal Growth
protocol: Plate neuronal cultures onto disposable Aclar towing culture substrates supported by the towing block.
Attach a disposable coverslip stationary substrate to the bottom of the stretching frame spanning all three lanes.
Allow plated neurons to extend axonal processes from the towing substrate onto the stationary substrate via growth cone extension.
Control displacement of the towing block to stretch the population of axons that bridge the substrates.
Prepare disposable towing culture substrates from Aclar film sheets.
Cut the substrates to approximately 0.5 x 2.5 cm.
Prepare stationary culture substrates for neuronal culture.
Mount the bioreactor chamber parallel to the linear motion table.
Fasten the towing rods extending from the bioreactor chamber to the linear motion table using an adaptor.
Program the step motor drive controller to control manipulation of the towing substrates.
Apply axonal stretch in a stepwise fashion by taking small displacement steps spaced by dwell times.
Sand the lower 1/3rd of the towing culture substrates on both sides using fine 1200-grit sandpaper.
Cut a 5 x 7cm piece of Aclar or use a No. 1 glass coverslip as the stationary substrate.
Clean the culture substrates with dilute Alconox solution and rinse thoroughly with purified dH2O.
Sterilize the culture substrates by immersion in 70% ethanol for 30 minutes.
Allow the sterilized substrates to air dry within a sterile tissue culture hood.
Clean the bioreactor chamber with dilute Alconox and autoclave sterilize within an autoclave container.
Immediately after autoclaving, transfer the bioreactor chamber to a sterile hood and allow it to air dry.
Glue the towing culture substrates to the towing block legs at the non-sanded portion using Silicon RTV and sterile cotton tipped swabs.
Glue the stationary culture substrate to the bottom of the bioreactor chamber using Silicon RTV and sterile cotton tipped swabs.
Remove excess glue and air pockets by gently depressing a dry swab against the glued substrates.
Leave the bioreactor under UV light within the hood for 2 full days prior to introducing neuronal cultures.
Lower the towing block legs to achieve a 2-3mm overlap between the tips of the sanded towing substrates and the stationary substrate.
Position the towing block at the starting position, with the towing rods retracted inside the bioreactor.
Tighten the immobilization screws to prevent movement of the towing rods prior to stretch growth.
Pool 1 mL of 10 μg/mL high molecular weight poly-d-lysine in serum-free media at the substrate interface area of each lane.
Allow the poly-d-lysine solution to adhere undisturbed for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse gently with dH2O three times, followed by a final rinse with culture media.
Pipette the rinsing solutions at the back of the lanes, farthest from the substrate interface.
Isolate Dorsal Root Ganglia explants (DRGs) from an E16 rat pup using a stereomicroscope.
Dilute the DRG explants into drops using petri dishes.
Collect 3-4 explants using a 100 μL pipette and plate onto the edge of the sanded towing culture substrate using a small puddle of media.
Attach the lid and transfer the bioreactor to an incubator for 1 hour or until cells adhere.
Fill the bioreactor with culture media at the point farthest from the explants to avoid dislodgment.
Incubate the bioreactor for a minimum of 5 days while neurons extend axonal processes onto the stationary substrate.
Fill reservoirs within the bioreactor with phosphate buffered saline.
Replace the culture media and fill the lanes to capacity.
Seat the bioreactor within the automated linear motion table.
Fasten the towing rod adaptor to the towing rods.
Jog the stage of the linear motion table using Si Programmer software to align with the towing rod adaptor.
Fasten the aligned towing rod adaptor to the stage.
Loosen the immobilization screws on the bioreactor chamber to allow free movement of the towing block.
Initiate stretch by taking 2 μm steps every 172 seconds, resulting in a net 1mm stretch over 24 hours.
Increase the stretch rate after one day by adjusting displacement or dwell time as needed.
Monitor culture media color for signs of acidification.
Partially change old media to minimize trauma to floating axons if further experimentation is required.
